bumpVersions.description: Chart.yaml version is the deploy trigger for Git-sourced charts (reconcileStrategy: ChartVersion), so bump it whenever a chart dependency changes

customManagers.description: Talos version, read from the factory installer image (the schematic ID stays). Matching only ghcr.io/siderolabs/installer left Talos frozen at v1.12.4 while Kubernetes kept bumping past what that Talos supports.

Versions Renovate cannot see on its own: image tags inside HelmRelease spec.values (flux only reads the chart reference, and values carry a bare tag: with the repository left to the chart default) and the tuppr TalosUpgrade/KubernetesUpgrade versions. Annotate the field with a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' line directly above it.

packageRules.description: Longhorn components must move together with the upstream chart; individual image bumps create unsupported manager and engine version skew.
Upgrade Longhorn only through its pinned chart dependency, in one reviewed release PR.

Talos-owned images: the installer and kubelet versions are tracked through siderolabs/talos and kubernetes/kubernetes (github-releases). factory.talos.dev is not a registry Renovate can list tags from, which showed up as a lookup failure on the dashboard.

linuxserver.io images: tags are <upstream version>[base]-ls<n> (12.2ubu2604-ls55, 4.0.20.3014-ls329, 5.1.4-r3-ls453). Since Jellyfin 12 there is no plain version tag, and docker versioning never changes a suffix, so a plain pin silently stops updating: pin the full tag. -ls<n> is a per-image counter that only grows, so it is the build part (regex versioning ignores revision without build) and a 4th upstream part is not needed for ordering. The base (ubuNNNN, alpine -rN, plex hash) is ignored so rebases do not stall updates; the narrow middle keeps branch and legacy tags (5.14-2.0.0.5344-ls15) out.

Talos and Kubernetes move in one PR: the tuppr TalosUpgrade/KubernetesUpgrade versions (merging is what upgrades the cluster), the installer image and the control-plane/kubelet images in talos/*.yaml (used for new installs) all change together. The Kubernetes images are found twice (docker datasource by the kubernetes manager, github-releases by the Talos custom managers), so both names are listed to keep them in this group. group.branchTopic is fixed because separateMultipleMinor (below) would otherwise put every minor stream on its own branch (minor-1.14-..., minor-1.37-...) and split Talos and Kubernetes into separate PRs; on one branch Renovate keeps the lowest step per dependency when several minors are pending (latest patch of the current minor, then the next minor), never a skip. A plain branchTopic or groupSlug still gets the per-minor prefix.
prBodyNotes: Merging this upgrades the cluster: tuppr rolls Talos node by node (health-gated on Ready nodes and healthy Longhorn volumes), then Kubernetes. Watch with `kubectl get talosupgrade,kubernetesupgrade -w`.

Talos must step through every minor and Kubernetes must stay inside the support matrix of the running Talos minor. If this PR moves the Talos minor, check https://docs.siderolabs.com/talos/latest/getting-started/support-matrix and raise the Kubernetes allowedVersions cap in renovate.json in the same PR if the new Talos supports a newer Kubernetes.

packageRules.description: Talos supports upgrading through each minor in turn, and talosctl upgrade-k8s moves Kubernetes one minor at a time; tuppr upgrades to exactly the version it is given. With two minors available Renovate must propose the next minor, not jump to the newest.
Kubernetes may not outrun the Talos support matrix (Talos v1.14 supports Kubernetes 1.33-1.37). Raise this cap together with the Talos minor that supports the next Kubernetes minor.
App image bumps: one PR per app, so a single bad bump cannot ride in with nine unrelated ones
Cluster-wide blast radius (storage, networking, TLS, Flux, Talos) is never automerged

install.yaml/crds.yaml under infrastructure/ are complete upstream manifests vendored whole. Bumping only the image tag leaves probes, RBAC and env vars at the old version - that is how MetalLB 0.16 broke the LoadBalancer (#298). Upgrade by re-vendoring the whole manifest.
Terraform providers keep the automerge they had under the old catch-all group
Chart version changes re-render a whole Helm release: always reviewed by hand
